title: Search Autocomplete (Typeahead)
intro: Design a real-time search typeahead system returning top-k query completions within 20 milliseconds as users type character-by-character.
objectives: Construct and optimize Trie (prefix tree) data structures with precomputed top-k suggestions.
Sample query frequencies using background MapReduce/Spark aggregation jobs.
Distribute prefix trees across Redis clusters using consistent hashing.
body:
### Data Structure: Trie with Precomputed Top-K
A standard Trie prefix search requires traversing from the prefix node down to all leaf nodes and sorting by frequency, which is far too slow for a 20ms SLA. **Optimization**: Store the top-5 most frequent search queries directly inside each Trie node:

```
          [root]
          /    \
        's'    'a'
        /        \
      'sy'       'ap'
 (top: 'system',  (top: 'apple',
  'sysdesign')     'app store')
```
Lookup latency drops to $O(L)$, where $L$ is the length of the query string (e.g. 3-5 characters), completely independent of total catalog size!
keyIdea: Precompute the top-k suggestions at every node in the prefix Trie. Query latency depends only on input prefix length, not dictionary size.

concepts.title: Frequency Sampling
concepts.body: Instead of logging every single keystroke, log 1 out of every 100 queries to calculate statistical frequency distributions with minimal I/O.

concepts.title: Client-Side Debouncing
concepts.body: Debouncing queries in JavaScript (e.g. 150ms delay) prevents flooding backend servers while the user is actively typing.

examples: Google instant search autocomplete and Amazon product typeahead.

quiz.prompt: How does storing precomputed top-k results at each Trie node improve lookup latency?
options: It compresses the Trie using gzip
It reduces query time complexity from traversing the entire subtree to O(L) where L is prefix length
It eliminates the need for RAM
quiz.explanation: Precomputing top-k results at each node allows instant lookup in O(L) time without traversing downstream descendants.
